description: The Inland Electronic Navigational Charts are the US Army Corps of Engineers' electronic charts of the inland waterway system, encoded to the Inland ENC 2.4 standard, an extension of the IHO S-57 transfer standard that adds features unique to rivers such as fleeting areas and lock walls. Charts show channels, navigation aids, locks, bridges, shorelines and other waterway features for voyage planning, electronic chart systems and GIS. The program, established in 2001, is run by USACE, whose inland system covers about 8,200 miles of rivers in 22 states with 276 lock chambers. Coverage is 7,260 charted miles in 20 river systems, including the Upper and Lower Mississippi, Ohio, Missouri, Illinois, Tennessee, Cumberland and Arkansas rivers, with more than 700 data products. Charts are free to download as S-57, shapefile and KML, with buoy overlays, XML catalogues and RSS feeds for automated updates, and as WMS, WFS and ArcGIS services; S-57 charts are updated monthly with Coast Guard notices to mariners. Caveats: USACE warns that features can be inaccurate because river conditions change, so the charts must be used with caution for navigation; paper chart books are sold separately. IENCs support network flow, capacity planning and hazard exposure studies of inland navigation and locks, and complement the National Waterway Network catalogued here.
